title: Round 38 New Jersey state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter register for New Jersey. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type, state, returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point; points are disclosed as points, never as boundaries, shorelines, lake polygons, or river centerlines.
selectionRules: Exact official name, compatible returned class/type, intended state, returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point must all identify the intended feature before VERIFIED=1.
The seeded coordinate is the GNIS primary point; it is never described as a boundary, shoreline, lake polygon, or river centerline.
A state screen that returns an empty array leaves the feature unseeded in that frame; it becomes a generalized context corridor or stays undisclosed-until-screened, never forced into a row.

Duplicate same-name records are separated by the official description locator where present (Bear Mountain, batch-12/round-28 rule), else by returned class/type and county; the loser is disclosed, never merged.

Records keyed to another state (Mount Frissell -> Massachusetts; Delaware River -> Delaware) are never seeded into this state's rows; the bordering frame either seeds its own-keyed record (delaware frame) or carries context only.

newjersey.title: New Jersey starter register (round 36, batch 18)
newjersey.frameNote: New Jersey batch-18 row: six populated-place anchors (Trenton capital, Newark, Jersey City, Elizabeth, Paterson, Camden) balanced with the Sussex High Point (per-id description "Highest elevation in NJ at 1803 feet."), Lake Hopatcong (Sussex-keyed Reservoir), and four water rows (Raritan, Passaic, Manasquan, Delaware and Raritan Canal). The Delaware River states=NJ screen returns an empty array and stays a corridor citing the Delaware-frame row (FEATURE_ID 217887).

identityDecisions.candidate: High Point name collision in New Jersey (Summit 877098 Sussex vs Populated Place 877099 Ocean)
identityDecisions.decision: Seed the Sussex County Summit; the Ocean County same-name populated place is not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The populated place is not a high point; the Summit point is not the state boundary or a survey marker coordinate.

identityDecisions.candidate: Lake Hopatcong records (Lake/Reservoir 877238 Sussex vs Populated Place 876215 Morris vs census division 2806109)
identityDecisions.decision: Seed the Sussex-keyed Reservoir record (per-ID: feature code 39004, 278 m, null description) under the Lake row class used by the UI; place and division records are not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The primary point is not the shoreline; Sussex is the returned primary county although the lake spans Morris too.

identityDecisions.decision: Corridor-only in the New Jersey frame; the national screen keys the Stream record to New Castle County, Delaware (217887), which main's delaware frame seeds as a row; same-name KS/NM rivers and the NY-keyed gorge record are not seeded here.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridor is not a channel centerline or the Delaware state boundary.

knownLimitations: Relief is labelled synthetic generalized morphology (no DEM claim); the labelled coast line is a synthetic context line, not a shoreline claim. GNIS points supply the rows, never the terrain, the corridors, or the frame rectangle.

The DomesticNames extract for NJ is produced by the arena-gnis-fetch CI workflow (sandbox egress cannot reach the S3 staging zips); this register's row assertions are enforced against the extract once CI lands it, and the gaznames_default REST per-ID checks plus Geocoder screens are the in-sandbox evidence of record.
New Jersey's High Point carries stored gaz_elevation 548 m against the official description's 1,803 feet (549.6 m rounding); both values are preserved as returned.
Delaware and Raritan Canal is stored as a Stream row (Geocoder type Streams & Canals) rather than introducing an untokenised Canal class row in the starter register.
Point coordinates are GNIS primary points: they are not boundaries, shorelines, lake polygons, river centerlines, municipal limits, or address geocodes.
